The largest IPO in history just landed — and the market fell anyway.

Anthropic opened at $111.50 a share Thursday and jumped about 27%, topping a $2 trillion value after an $81 billion offering — the biggest IPO ever (CNBC, Nov. 19).

But one hot debut couldn't carry Wall Street: the Dow was down around 800 points in afternoon trading and the S&P 500 headed for a sixth straight losing day (Yahoo Finance, Nov. 19).

Why it's your money: the S&P 500 anchors most 401(k)s and target-date funds, so a six-day slide quietly trims retirement balances — and Canadian funds hold these same US tech names too.

My take: when the year's biggest success story can't stop the bleeding, the worry isn't one stock — it's how much of the market now rides on the AI trade.

Has this stretch of red changed how you're investing?
